sanskrit_verse:
सहसा क्रियते कर्म यत्किंचिद् बलदर्पितैः।
तत् साहसम् इति प्रोक्तं सहो बलम् इहोच्यते॥
transliteration: sahasā kriyate karma yatkiṃcid baladarpitaiḥ | tat sāhasam iti proktaṃ saho balam ihocyate ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Any action performed impulsively by those intoxicated with power is termed 'sāhasa'; indeed, 'saha' denotes the misuse of strength.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from alignment with consciousness, not force
Causation originates in misidentification with power
Capacity-based responsibility is diminished under intoxication of dominance
Restoration requires realignment with dharmic capacity
executable_legal_axioms: IF actor exhibits behavior driven by intoxication of power THEN classify act as 'sāhasa'
IF classified as 'sāhasa' THEN initiate consciousness-realigning restoration protocol
IF authority exercised without dharmic grounding THEN trigger capacity-restoration mechanism
IF imbalance detected in causal agency THEN assign completion process to restore integrity
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, any exercise of authority unmoored from dharma must be recognized as 'sāhasa'. The threshold of responsibility lies not in intent but in alignment with cosmic order. Courts must activate restorative frameworks that realign the actor's consciousness rather than impose punitive measures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that 'sāhasa' stems from erroneous identification with brute force. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how intoxication leads to distortion of dharma. Responsibility is proportional to clarity of consciousness. Since reality is non-punitive, justice operates through correction of energetic and perceptual imbalances.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate pratyāhāra-based withdrawal from externalized power dependencies
Assign svādhyāya-based self-inquiry into source of distorted strength
Implement dāna-yoga to redirect excess energy toward dharmic service
Establish śama-dama practices to stabilize emotional-intellectual balance
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law flows directly from His Avataric Intelligence. Dharma is restored when consciousness displaces coercion. Reality remains non-punitive; only misaligned energies require adjustment. Consciousness alone is the ultimate judge.
